plain.li: [years] Founding day. I counted the faces at the long table and couldn't help counting the missing ones too.
Founding day. We walked the old boundary after supper, and it's a lot further than it used to be.

warm.li: Founding day. I thanked the ones who were here first, and the ones who came after.

blunt.li: Founding day. Ate well. Didn't make a speech. Good.

cheerful.li: Founding day! Someone made a cake in the shape of the first shelter, roof and all.

gloomy.li: Founding day. I keep thinking about the first night, and how little we knew.

cold.li: Founding day. We've lasted longer than most settlements out here.

plain.li: [!new] Harvest day. We ate outside at the edge of the fields, the way it was done the first year.

warm.li: [!new] Harvest day. I took a plate out to the ones still working the last rows.

blunt.li: [!new] Harvest day. Ate. Slept. Fields tomorrow.

cheerful.li: [!new] Harvest day! I wore a crown of straw all evening and wouldn't take it off.

gloomy.li: [!new] Harvest day. I ate as if the next harvest might not come.

cold.li: [!new] Harvest day. Morale is up, and morale brings in the next harvest.

plain.li: [!new] First snow of the winter. Stacked the last of the wood under cover and stood watching it come down.

warm.li: [!new] First snow. I made sure everyone had dry socks before the games started.

cheerful.li: [!new] First snow! I built a snow figure of the council and gave it a very serious face.

gloomy.li: [!new] The first snow. Months of this now.

cold.li: [!new] First snow. The games are a useful way to get the cold season started without complaint.

plain.li: Kept the day for {DEAD}. Someone put {DEAD}'s favorite food on the table, and the plate sat there untouched all supper.
[years] {DEAD}'s day again. The newcomers asked who {DEAD} was, and three of us answered at once.

warm.li: The day {DEAD} died. I told the children one of {DEAD}'s stories, the way {DEAD} used to tell it.

cheerful.li: We laughed about {DEAD} at supper today. {DEAD} would have laughed loudest.

gloomy.li: The day {DEAD} died. The grave's grown over a bit more. I tidied it.

cold.li: {DEAD}'s day. The colony is weaker without {DEAD}. I've said that every year, and it's still true.

plain.li: Our wedding day. {OTHER_nameDef} and I walked out to where we said our vows and stood there a while.

warm.li: Our wedding day. I told {OTHER_nameDef} I'd do it all again, the bad weeks too.

blunt.li: Our day. {OTHER_nameDef} and me. Still good.

cheerful.li: Our wedding day! {OTHER_nameDef} and I danced at supper, and this time we didn't knock anything over.

gloomy.li: Our wedding day. Another year we've both lived through. I'll take it.

cold.li: Our wedding day. {OTHER_nameDef} remains the best decision I've made here.

plain.li: The day {OTHER_nameDef} arrived. We sat up and talked about that first week, and how thin everyone was.

warm.li: It's the day {OTHER_nameDef} came to us. I saved {OTHER_objective} the best seat without saying why.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef}'s arrival day. Good day, that was.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef}'s day! I told everyone the story of how {OTHER_pronoun} turned up, with improvements.

gloomy.li: The day {OTHER_nameDef} came. So many of us from that year are gone now. Not {OTHER_nameDef}, thank goodness.

cold.li: The anniversary of {OTHER_nameDef}'s arrival. {OTHER_nameDef} has proved worth taking in.

plain.li: {NAME}. Somebody brought out a jar they'd been saving, and we finished it.

warm.li: {NAME}. I helped in the kitchen so the cooks could sit down and eat with everyone.

blunt.li: {NAME}. Good food. Too much of it. No complaints.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! I ate until I had to loosen my belt, and then I had dessert.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. Good food, good company. I tried not to think about tomorrow.

cold.li: {NAME}. The cooks outdid themselves, which I'll remember next time rations are set.

plain.li: {NAME}. Cleaned the grave markers and read every name aloud.

warm.li: {NAME}. I left a small stone on each grave, the way someone once did for my family.

cheerful.li: {NAME}. We told the best story we had about each of them, and laughed more than I expected.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. The names are starting to blur, which is the worst part.

cold.li: {NAME}. I keep my own list of the dead. It matched the colony's this year.

plain.li: {NAME}. Lost the tug-of-war, won the stone toss, and pulled a muscle in between.

warm.li: {NAME}. Helped the children with their race and let them win, mostly.

blunt.li: {NAME}. Won one. Lost three. Ate well after.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! I came second in the footrace, which is the best I've ever done.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. Everyone laughed a lot today. I hope we remember it next bad week.

cold.li: {NAME}. I studied how each of them competes. It tells you a lot about a person.

plain.li: {NAME}. Mended a shirt, slept an hour, and talked to people I usually only pass.

warm.li: {NAME}. Spent the day with friends, with nowhere else to be.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! I lay on my back and watched the clouds until I fell asleep.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. A day off, and I spent it thinking. Should have worked.

cold.li: {NAME}. Rested, as required. I'll be sharper tomorrow.

plain.li: [clean] The day we beat {ENEMY}. I cleaned my weapon and thought about how close it was.

warm.li: [fallen] The day we lost {DEAD}. I went round and sat with everyone who'd been there.

blunt.li: [fallen] {DEAD}'s battle day. Visited the grave. Said nothing. Didn't need to.

cheerful.li: [nemesis] The day {ENEMY} fell! We toasted it at supper, loudly.

gloomy.li: [nemesis] The day {ENEMY} fell. I still wake up sometimes thinking {ENEMY} is out there.

cold.li: [nemesis] Anniversary of {ENEMY}'s end. A threat removed. I don't miss it.

plain.li: [self] My birthday. I was given a cup of something warm and an afternoon off.

warm.li: [self] My birthday. I spent it with the people I love, which is all I wanted.

blunt.li: [friend] {OTHER_nameDef}'s birthday. Gave {OTHER_objective} my good knife. Don't tell anyone I'm soft.

cheerful.li: [self] My birthday! They all sang, and I sang along, loudest.

gloomy.li: [self] Another birthday. I'm still here, which is more than I'd bet on.

cold.li: [friend] {OTHER_nameDef}'s birthday. A small gift costs little and keeps a friendship in good order.

plain.li: [years] Founding day, {YEARS} years in the {PLACE}. {A_nameDef} has been asked to tell the story of the first winter, and has agreed, at length.
Founding day. {A_nameDef} has dug out the old shovel from the first season and hung it over the door.

blunt.li: Founding day. {A_nameDef} says the colony made it this far by being too stubborn to leave, and would like that on a banner.

cheerful.li: Founding day! {A_nameDef} has been greeting everyone with the date, as if they might have forgotten.

plain.li: Harvest day. {A_nameDef} brought a basket in from the fields this morning and set it in the middle of the table.
[years] Harvest day again, {YEARS} years on. {A_nameDef} is out early checking the rows, as if the day depended on it.

warm.li: Harvest day. {A_nameDef} has been round thanking everyone who ever pulled a weed in those fields.

gloomy.li: Harvest day. {A_nameDef} remembers how close the first crop came to failing, and isn't letting anyone forget.

plain.li: The first snow of the winter is coming down, and {A_nameDef} has already called off the afternoon's work, on nobody's authority but {A_possessive} own.
[years] The first snow again. {YEARS} winters on, {A_nameDef} is still the first one out to test whether it's sticky enough for snowballs.

warm.li: The first snow of the winter. {A_nameDef} has been round with extra blankets before anyone asked.

blunt.li: First snow. {A_nameDef} wants the games over before anyone catches cold.

plain.li: [clean] On this day the colony saw off {ENEMY}. {A_nameDef} has been retelling it to the ones who weren't here for it.

warm.li: [fallen] On this day {ENEMY} came, and {DEAD} did not come home. {A_nameDef} has asked everyone to say {DEAD}'s name once today.

cheerful.li: [clean] The day the colony beat {ENEMY}! {A_nameDef} has started the story already, and it gets better every year.

cold.li: [nemesis] The day {ENEMY} was brought down. {A_nameDef} marks it every year as a lesson in what the colony can do.

plain.li: [years] {YEARS} years since {DEAD} died. {A_nameDef} has polished {DEAD}'s old tools and set them out on the bench for the day.
Today the colony keeps the day of {DEAD}'s death. {A_nameDef} will tell {DEAD}'s story at supper, as is done.

cheerful.li: Today the colony remembers {DEAD}. {A_nameDef} wants it to be a day of {DEAD}'s best stories, and has started with the funniest.

gloomy.li: The day {DEAD} died. {A_nameDef} has said very little since dawn, and the others have let {A_objective} be.

plain.li: [years] {YEARS} years married today, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}. The colony has set them the best seats at supper whether they like it or not.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}'s wedding day. Someone has hung a garland over their door in the night.
[winter] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}'s wedding day, in the deep cold. They've been given the warmest corner of the hall.
It's {NAME}. The kitchen has been busy since before dawn, and the smell has reached every room.
[years] {NAME}, kept {YEARS} years now. {A_nameDef} remembers the first one, when the feast was mostly bread.

warm.li: {NAME} today. {A_nameDef} wants a place laid for everyone, including whoever's on watch.

plain.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} has cleared the path to the graves and set a lamp at the gate.
[winter] {NAME} in the snow. {A_nameDef} has swept the snow off each grave marker so the names can be read.

warm.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} has asked that each of the dead be named at supper by someone who knew them.

plain.li: {NAME}. The workbenches are quiet, and {A_nameDef} has been seen sitting in the sun with nothing in {A_possessive} hands.
[winter] {NAME} in the cold. The colony will rest indoors today, close together and warm.

cheerful.li: It's {NAME}! {A_nameDef} has declared a contest for the longest nap, and entered first.

plain.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} has chalked lines across the yard and is explaining the rules to anyone who'll listen.
[years] {NAME} again, {YEARS} years running. {A_nameDef} has been training for the stone toss and denies it.

cheerful.li: {NAME}! {A_nameDef} has hung a prize over the door. It's a turnip, but it's a very good turnip.

plain.li: {A_nameDef}'s birthday today. Someone has left a small gift on {A_possessive} bed.
[summer] {A_nameDef}'s birthday, on a warm day. The colony may eat outside to mark it.

cheerful.li: It's {A_nameDef}'s birthday! There will be singing, and {A_nameDef} has been warned.

plain.li: [years] {YEARS} years ago today, {A_nameDef} came to the colony, one of the first.
It's the day {A_nameDef} first came to the colony, when there wasn't much of it yet.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} counted the buildings that weren't there on the colony's first day.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} who had been the first to dig in the {PLACE}.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} compared calluses from the harvest.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} which crops {A_pronoun} would plant more of next year.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about the snow, and how deep it got last winter.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} whether {B_pronoun} had ever seen a winter as bad as the first one here.
[fallen] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} went over what {DEAD} did on the day of the battle, and what it cost.
[clean] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} what {A_pronoun} remembers of the day {ENEMY} came.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} told each other what they would have said to {DEAD}, given the chance.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about the last time they saw {DEAD}.
[couple] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} remembered who cried at their wedding.
[!couple] {B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} what the wedding feast had been like.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} how glad {A_pronoun} was that {B_nameDef} came.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} remembered what the colony looked like when {B_nameDef} first saw it.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued about how old {B_nameDef} really is.
{A_nameDef} wished {B_nameDef} a happy birthday and asked what {B_pronoun} wanted most this year.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued over which dish at {NAME} was the best.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} which dish of {NAME} {A_pronoun} would remember longest.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} went through the names of the dead together on {NAME}.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about the first person {A_pronoun} saw buried here.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spent part of {NAME} talking about nothing in particular.
[winter] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} swapped stories of worse winters on {NAME}.
{A_nameDef} cheerfully accused {B_nameDef} of cheating in the games on {NAME}.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} agreed to train together for next year's {NAME}.
[way:feast] {A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} to help set the tables for {NAME} in the morning.
[way:remembrance] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about who they would name tomorrow on {NAME}.
[way:games] {A_nameDef} challenged {B_nameDef} to beat {A_objective} at tomorrow's games.
[way:rest] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that tomorrow, for once, the work can wait.
